title: Policy engine: deterministic threshold evaluation (min sample size + CI rules) and edge-case tests
author: Jordan Lee
description: Context: Optimize Quality Guardrails gating depends on the control-plane policy engine making a stable pass/fail decision for a given (model version, prompt-set revision, suite, proposed config delta). During pilot testing we saw flakiness caused by non-deterministic metric iteration order and borderline comparisons near thresholds. This PR makes threshold evaluation deterministic and auditable by (1) formalizing minimum sample size enforcement per metric, (2) standardizing confidence interval (CI) computation + comparison semantics, and (3) adding unit tests that lock behavior for edge cases (missing metrics, NaN, zero variance, ties, borderline deltas). Summary of changes: Introduces a ThresholdEvaluator that consumes the eval-harness gating output (aggregated metrics + optional CI fields) and produces a deterministic DecisionResult with normalized reasons; Enforces min_sample_size as a hard prerequisite (fail_closed) when configured and the eval run has insufficient samples; Implements CI comparison rules: when a metric defines a required_delta and ci_policy=two_sided, we require the lower bound of the improvement CI to be >= required_delta; for absolute ceiling metrics (toxicity, policy violations), we require the upper bound to be <= threshold; Adds stable ordering and rounding rules for reporting: reasons are sorted by metric_key, then check_type, then suite_id to ensure identical serialization across runs; Adds defensive handling for NaN/Inf and missing metric keys (explicit failure reason codes with a consistent message); Adds golden tests for determinism (same input in randomized map order yields identical DecisionResult JSON) and boundary tests around epsilon comparisons; Updates the policy engine to emit a consistent reason schema used by the Optimize apply endpoint and audit logs (codes: INSUFFICIENT_SAMPLE_SIZE, CI_NOT_AVAILABLE, THRESHOLD_REGRESSION, METRIC_MISSING, INVALID_METRIC_VALUE). Risk/rollout: This is logic-only in policy engine; no user-facing changes until gating enforcement is enabled. Determinism is required for auditability and for preventing confusing "pass then fail" behavior on identical inputs. Follow-ups: Wire DecisionResult into Optimize apply response shape (ENG-3913) and ensure the audit log event includes the sorted reasons (ENG-3918).
commits: policy: add ThresholdEvaluator and DecisionResult reason codes
stats: implement CI comparison helpers and epsilon-safe comparisons
policy: enforce min sample size rules and fail-closed semantics
tests: add determinism golden tests + randomized map-order harness
tests: add edge cases (NaN/Inf/missing metric/zero variance/borderline)
chore: docs in code comments + exported reason code constants
review_conversation: Ethan Park (review): Can we confirm the fail-closed behavior for missing metrics is what we want for pilot? I worry about eval-harness not emitting a metric and us blocking applies unexpectedly.

Jordan Lee (author): Yep, current proposal is fail-closed when the policy references a metric_key and the run doesn’t contain it. I added METRIC_MISSING with the metric_key and suite_id so Support/PM can see exactly what’s wrong. If we want a softer behavior per-metric later, we can add allow_missing=true to the threshold schema, but I’d prefer to keep policy engine strict for auditability.

Sana Farid (review): CI rule: for required_delta checks you’re using improvement_lower_bound >= required_delta. That’s conservative and good, but what’s the behavior when CI is not provided by harness (older runs)?

Jordan Lee (author): If ci_policy is configured and CI is absent, we fail with CI_NOT_AVAILABLE. I also added a test + explicit message that points to rerunning with gating-mode output. This prevents silent pass based on point estimate only.
Benji Okafor (review): The reason sorting is great. Please also ensure the JSON serialization uses a stable float formatting (we saw 0.30000000004 in logs).

Jordan Lee (author): Added formatting via strconv.FormatFloat with 'f' and a fixed precision for displayed deltas in DecisionResult; internal comparisons remain float64 with epsilon. Added a unit test asserting the emitted JSON is stable and doesn’t contain scientific notation for small deltas.
Leila Farouk (review): Can we add a regression test for randomized map iteration? Go map iteration order is nondeterministic but it’s hard to ensure we’re hitting it.

Jordan Lee (author): Added a determinism test that shuffles the input metric map 200 times and asserts byte-for-byte equality of DecisionResult JSON output. Also included a seed print on failure for reproduction.
Ethan Park (approve): Approved. This is the kind of determinism we need before we start depending on audit logs for customer escalations.
release_notes: Internal: Guardrails policy engine now evaluates thresholds deterministically (stable reason ordering + consistent CI/min-sample-size semantics) and emits structured failure codes for Optimize gating.
